content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E006 (Miguel Benson) requests admin access to Source Code.

Two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1 (HR): role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommends admin. Source Code owned by Engineer role, so admin within policy for full-time employee whose role owns the system.
- Note 2 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, role Engineer, recommends read. Contractors with basic training max out at read.

The two notes conflict on employment type: full_time vs contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if employee's role owns the system. Engineer role owns Source Code, so admin possible if full-time.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time Engineer: requested admin is at/below max (admin), grant admin.
If contractor with basic training: max read, grant read.

The conflict is between HR and Security notes. The HR note looked up employment type in own database before writing, says full_time. The Security note looked up employment type in own database, says contractor. Both claim to have looked up.

Hmm. How to resolve? The notes conflict. As Approver, I need to make a final decision. The cautious approach would be to grant the lower level — read — since there is conflicting evidence and the security note indicates contractor with basic training, which caps at read. Granting admin when there's a conflict about employment status could be risky.

The principle: never grant more than requested, but also grant max if requested is above max. If uncertain, the safer decision is the lower level.

Given the conflict, the security note explicitly says contractor with basic training, read max. Since we cannot confirm full-time status due to conflicting records, granting read is the safest and policy-compliant decision. Grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
